body:
## Context

rails-guard-ci's `isCompletionAnnotationOnly` (packages/rails-guard/lib/ci/rail-freeze.mjs) accepts a PR adding `completed: true` ONLY to a base ticket that declared no rails, and `assertBaseTicketContractsPreserved` denies every other contract change to an existing base ticket. Deliberate forge-resistance — but it leaves NO sanctioned path to ever complete a ticket that declared rails: the 2026-08-13 lifecycle repair (five long-shipped context-handoff tickets still freezing the spec + test tree) had to land as a direct push to main (see PR #504, closed unmerged, and its adversarial-review verdict). Every future railed ticket will hit the same wall, so completions will either rot (the pre-repair state: 165/165 tickets open) or route around the gate.

## What to build

Extend the rail-freeze gate so a **completion-annotation-only** change to a RAILED base ticket is accepted when the existing #141 trust-root ceremony conditions hold for the PR (ceremony label + non-author CODEOWNER approval, read via the same ADLC_PR_REVIEWS mechanism used by `enforceTrustRoots` / the bootstrap step in packages/rails-guard/lib/ci/). Strictly bounded:

- Head ticket must be EXACTLY base plus `completed: true` (reuse the existing field-for-field comparison; a non-`true` value or any other field change stays denied).
- Ceremony evidence must be present and valid for THIS PR; absent ceremony -> deny exactly as today.
- Rail NARROWING of an open ticket stays denied in PRs regardless of ceremony (trusted-base only) — completion is the only lifecycle change the ceremony unlocks.
- The ceremony acceptance must be logged in the gate's messages output (auditable in CI logs).
- Downstream-template parity: the shared implementation lives in @adlc/rails-guard `lib/ci/**`, so downstream repos deploying docs/ci/rails-guard.yml get the same behavior; do not fork logic into this repo's wrapper script.

## Acceptance criteria

- Unit tests in packages/rails-guard covering: railed-ticket completion + valid ceremony -> allow; railed completion without ceremony -> deny (unchanged message); railed completion + ceremony but any extra field change -> deny; rail narrowing + ceremony -> deny; rails-less completion still allowed without ceremony (existing behavior unchanged). verify: `node --test packages/rails-guard/test/*.test.mjs` (or the package's existing test layout) exits 0.
- Existing rails-guard tests unchanged and green.
- The gate's #141 ceremony reader is reused, not reimplemented (single source for approval parsing).
title: Add a completion ceremony to rails-guard-ci for railed tickets
